Limits
No boards or instruments were attached. Source compilation is not a full GNU Arm runtime link or verified flash image. Timer/DMA interrupt execution, real SPI setup/hold, 200 us completion time including CRC and every-fifth-scan control work, ADC aperture skew, analog behavior, and physical shutdown latency require scope checks. title: Earlier communication contract v2
text:
Shared MCU SPI bus
The STM32 owns SPI1 at 1 MHz, mode 0, MSB first. PA1 selects the MCP3204; PA4 selects the FPGA. PA5/PA7/PA6 are shared SCK/MOSI/MISO. Only one chip select may be low. The FPGA releases MISO when PA4 is high, including during ADC transactions.
TIM6 releases one scan every 200 us (5 kHz). DMA1 channel 2/request 1 receives SPI1 data and channel 3/request 1 transmits it. Each ADC channel gets a separate 24-clock transaction: CH0 current, CH1 primary Hall, and optionally CH2 reference Hall. ADC CS is high for at least 1 us between conversions. These sequential readings belong to the same scan; they are not simultaneous. Then the MCU exchanges one 8-byte FPGA packet, with at least 2 us CS lead/trail guards. DMA completion interrupts advance the transactions. A DMA error, stalled SPI, or scan overrun removes permit and halts acquisition until reset.
The FPGA consumes one new measured/requested-current pair per valid packet, nominally 5 kHz. The MCU estimates height and runs its position/motion controller every fifth completed ADC scan (1 kHz). The requested current computed on that scan is sent in the following FPGA transaction. HTML generation and UART traffic run in the foreground while acquisition/control runs in interrupts.

Eight-byte frames
Fields are explicitly packed big-endian. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE uses polynomial 0x1021, initial 0xffff, no reflection/final XOR, over bytes 0-5, stored high byte first in bytes 6-7. Check vector: 123456789 -> 0x29b1. This wire format is incompatible with the old 16-byte design; rebuild both devices.

Measurement and target are absolute ADC codes, including current zero offset. The compiled FPGA ceiling is in project_config.svh; the firmware’s hard_limit_counts must agree. Current PI gains also live in that FPGA configuration, with Kp Q8.8 in 0-4096 and Ki Q8.8 in 0-1024; Ki includes the 200 us sample period. They no longer occupy packet fields. Example gains remain zero until measured and tuned.
The reply is a coherent snapshot frozen at CS assertion, acknowledging the previous transaction. MCU feedback verifies that previous sequence after the first exchange; it does not interpret the reply as acknowledgment of the packet still on the wire. Local ADC data is retained separately and never overwritten by FPGA telemetry. A missing acknowledgment, CRC/bounds failure, or missed 200 us acquisition deadline trips MCU control.
The FPGA rejects short/overlong packets, reserved flags, bad CRCs, out-of-range values, and immediately repeated sequence numbers. Rejected packets cannot update PI or refresh the watchdog. Every accepted packet updates the current PI once. Fifty milliseconds without a fresh command while enabled latches a timeout fault. This is an MCU-command watchdog, not independent proof of ADC electrical health. Frozen but plausible analog readings need physical diagnosis and the independent comparator/interlock.
Fault bits: 0 external interlock, 1 measured overcurrent, 2 command timeout; bits 3-7 reserved. Clearing requires a fresh disabled packet, healthy external interlock, and measured current below the compiled limit. Clear and arm are separate actions. Permit and external fault directly remove gate permission without waiting for another serial packet.

title: Earlier communication contract v2
text:
ESP8266 to MCU
The unchanged course bridge uses USART1, 125000 baud, 8N1, and /REQ:<route>\n (CRLF also accepted). Exact routes are empty/root, arm, stop, clear, modegap, modeamp, up, and down. The response is one complete HTML document. Refresh points at root once per second so commands are not repeated by refresh. A recognized request renews a 5-second browser lease; expiry is checked in the interrupt control path. Web STOP removes MCU permit immediately after parsing. Physical E-stop remains independent of communications.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
Position sensing and motion
Gap is positive downward from the coil. The local estimator is
gap_mm = c0 + c1*H1_counts + c2*H2_counts + c3*measured_current_A.
Set hall_sensors=1 for CH0/CH1 scans with current compensation and c2=0; use hall_sensors=2 for CH0/CH1/CH2 scans and the full calibrated fit. tools/calibrate.py --hall-sensors 1 supports a single-Hall CSV without a second Hall column. Independent holdout validation is still required. Symmetry and opposite sensor orientation do not guarantee electromagnetic field cancellation; fitted coefficients must establish the actual polarity and response.
The MCP3204 offers pseudo-differential inputs: IN- must stay within 100 mV of ground. Two DRV5055 outputs centered near half supply cannot be connected as a differential pair. Consequently this implementation reads both channels single-ended and combines them digitally. True differential acquisition would require suitable analog conditioning or a different ADC. See section 4.1 of the manufacturer datasheet.
The MCU runs every fifth scan with e = measured_gap - ramped_target:
Irequest = clamp(Ihover + Kp*e + Kd*filtered_velocity + integral, 0, Imax).
Positive error or falling motion requests more lift. Derivative acts on measurement, with initialization to avoid kick; integral uses conditional anti-windup. Gap commands are bounded and slew-limited. The supplied example interval is 8-10 mm with 1 mm/s target motion and a 10 mm/s filtered velocity trip. These values require measurements; they are not calibrated plant limits. Current-test mode ramps current separately with the object supported. Additional permanent magnets and any separate velocity loop require characterization before use.
ADC channels are sampled sequentially, with current first. Packet pairing preserves the scan association, but cannot remove interchannel aperture skew or PWM ripple. Measure compensation error with the target clamped while changing coil current. Moving averages, coil-off sampling, lookup tables, and alternate optical/ultrasonic sensing remain possible future changes, not claimed features.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
Current controller and shutdown
The FPGA updates PI once for each accepted fresh current pair, nominally every 200 us. Kp and Ki use Q8.8; Ki already includes 0.0002 s. Signed products/sums and the integrator are bounded; duty clamps to 0-1080 of 1200 clocks (90%). Seven arithmetic stages finish in less than 0.3 us at 24 MHz. Duty changes at PWM boundaries. Disabling clears PI history. Compiled gains live in project_config.svh and must be tuned for the new update period.
Serial CRC takes 48 clocks (2 us); registered validation adds a few more clocks. Status is refreshed every 64 FPGA clocks and frozen for an SPI transaction. Faults latch for external interlock, measured overcurrent, and 50 ms without fresh commands. Invalid or repeated packets cannot refresh the watchdog or repeat an integrator update. Safe disabled commands can clear faults; enabling and clearing are separate actions. See the wire contract.
MCU permit and external fault gate the physical output immediately, independently of packet processing. ADC DMA errors/stalls/overruns remove permit and halt acquisition until reset. Telemetry checksum or previous-sequence acknowledgment failure also stops MCU control. The separate comparator/E-stop is essential because a plausible stuck ADC code is not digitally distinguishable from a steady input.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Measurements
Use a fixed jig and known gap reference. Log gap_mm,hall1,hall2,current_a rows in CSV for two sensors, or gap_mm,hall1,current_a for one sensor; data/calibration-format.csv gives the header. Measure actual current, not just commanded current. Sample a grid of gaps and currents spanning the proposed operating interval, with repeated measurements after reversing each sweep. Include coil-only baseline, object orientation, supply, temperature, sensor mount dimensions, and ADC filter components in the experiment notes.
Use a second independently collected sweep for holdout validation. Randomly splitting adjacent samples from one stationary measurement understates error. Repeat across relevant coil temperatures and several current trajectories. Hold the object fixed during current steps to quantify how much coil-field change leaks into estimated position. A static fit may pass while sequential-channel transient error makes feedback unusable.
The local affine model is a practical first model, not a physical cancellation guarantee. Nonmonotonic or degenerate sensor responses require a change of placement, object, sensitivity, or estimator. A table/nonlinear estimator is a future design change if the local fit fails; it is not silently implemented by the calibration script. Restrict the committed gap/current interval to where this model has been validated.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Fit and validate
python -m pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python tools/calibrate.py data/raw/training.csv data/raw/holdout.csv --hall-sensors 2
# For CH0 current + CH1 Hall only (hall2 column may be omitted):
python tools/calibrate.py data/raw/training-single.csv data/raw/holdout-single.csv --hall-sensors 1
The script normalizes inputs, checks matrix rank and conditioning, fits least squares, prints training/holdout errors, and emits candidate hall_c coefficients only when numerical acceptance passes. It rejects near-rail Hall samples and a holdout current/gap range outside the training range. It does not change firmware or enable outputs. Save reviewed coefficients and measured validity ranges in config.c; preserve data deliberately under data/results when suitable for the public repository. Files under data/raw are ignored by default.
Current conversion is I=(ADC-current_zero)/counts_per_amp. Fit zero/gain against an independent meter over the intended range. Convert an absolute trip current into round(current_zero + counts_per_amp * Itrip) and choose a conservative threshold accounting for uncertainty. Keep the FPGA compiled ceiling, comparator, and firmware cap consistent. Current PI gains are compiled in fpga/rtl/project_config.svh; they are no longer sent over SPI. The runtime cap should remain below the physical trip threshold.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Gains and practical limits
The height loop uses mm, A, and seconds: Kp has A/mm; Kd has A·s/mm; Ki has A/(mm·s). Begin with Ki zero. Verify lift direction on a supported object before release. The current loop uses ADC counts and PWM ticks, with Ki already multiplied by 0.0002 s. Quantizing a small Ki to zero changes loop behavior; verify the quantized loop rather than only the floating-point design.
Tune around one measured equilibrium. The force model may change significantly with gap. hover_a is a constant bias in this implementation; there is no unvalidated gain scheduling or feedforward lookup. The feasible height interval may therefore be smaller than the candidate 8-10 mm values. Browser targets and fault limits must be updated to match the tested interval. Sampling rate, delay, sensor filtering, coil decay, object mass, and lateral/orientation motion all affect stability.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 1. Establish sensing feasibility before a parts commitment
text:
1. Establish sensing feasibility before a parts commitment
Mount the candidate coil and actual object at known gaps using nonmagnetic spacers. Measure both Hall voltages with no object, with the object, and at multiple coil currents. Choose sensor orientation/sensitivity so signals remain in their linear range and neither clips. Measure whether object position remains distinguishable after coil-current effects and noise are included. Sweep the gap in both directions to expose hysteresis, rotation, and ambiguous responses. For a plain steel sphere, explicitly check the current-dependent magnetization model rather than adopting the permanent-magnet assumptions.
Acceptance: at least one contiguous operating interval has repeatable position estimates with independent holdout RMSE ≤0.25 mm and worst error ≤0.5 mm. These are proposed design thresholds; revise the committed specification with the team/instructor before proposal submission if feasibility measurements require it. Stop expanding the system if observability fails; change geometry/sensor arrangement/object first.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
2. Characterize coil and driver
Measure coil DC resistance cold and hot, inductance or current step response, lift force versus current and gap, current needed to support the measured object mass, and temperature rise. Select supply, switch, clamp, wiring, fuse, current cap, and mechanical clearance from those measurements. Establish a continuous-duty current rating or add a thermal cutoff in the physical interlock. The supplied code does not measure coil temperature.
Acceptance: lift exceeds weight with operating margin throughout the chosen interval; thermal and electrical ratings support the intended demo duration. Document tau=L/R, maximum current rise/decay rates, Pcoil=I²R, switch/shunt dissipation, and clamp voltage. Do not power the coil through the development board or a solderless breadboard power rail.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 3. Verify digital paths with coil power disconnected
text:
3. Verify digital paths with coil power disconnected
Check bridge switches open and every jumper by continuity. Program default-disabled devices. Confirm the UART baud and complete HTML. Capture the shared MCU SPI bus and both chip selects: mode 0, clock rates, CS guards, 64-bit host frames, CRC byte ordering, 24 ADC clocks, channel order, and CS high interval. Apply known analog voltages to the ADC channels. Compare raw telemetry against a meter. A plausible constant ADC code is not sufficient proof that an ADC is connected.
Acceptance: decoded measurements match applied voltages and the C/SV packet tests. Scope MCU ADC CS, sample_debug, and PWM to verify 5 kHz scans/accepted packets, 20 kHz PWM, and interchannel timing; output remains low during reset, programming, power loss, and disconnected permit/interlock.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 4. Calibrate and prove the physical cutoff
text:
4. Calibrate and prove the physical cutoff
Support the object; initially replace the coil with a resistive load if suitable for the driver. Calibrate current zero and gain against a meter, including low-current output headroom. Compute the firmware absolute code limit and FPGA compiled ceiling from actual calibration; account for tolerances. Check the inline shunt measures flyback current. Set and measure the comparator threshold/hysteresis independently. Operate the E-stop and break each interlock wire while monitoring the actual MOSFET gate.
Acceptance: no unintended pulse at startup; physical fault removes gate drive promptly even if the MCU and FPGA are halted. Record the measured gate-off delay and coil-current decay separately. Only then set power_stage_ready=true and LEV_COMMISSIONED=1 with low supply/current limits, still supported mechanically. Keep calibration_ready=false.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
5. Tune the inner current loop
Select current-test mode while stopped. Start at zero target. Begin with Ki zero and small Kp; increase until current follows small supported-load steps without sustained ringing. Add a modest Ki to remove steady error. Convert gains into the documented Q8.8 per-sample units. Examine response across PWM duty and supply voltage. Avoid integral gains below one representable step unless a different fixed-point scale is implemented.
Acceptance: no sustained oscillation, no saturation under nominal commands, bounded overshoot, and measured response sufficiently faster than the intended position loop. Sweep current through the allowed range and verify the cap. Test MCU cable removal, identical frozen packets, checksum errors, missed updates, ADC disconnect, comparator trip, permit loss, and E-stop. An ADC disconnect can yield a plausible stuck value; the physical cutoff remains necessary. Retain scope captures, not just a pass checkbox.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 6. Fit Hall calibration and tune the position loop
text:
6. Fit Hall calibration and tune the position loop
Follow docs/calibration.md with current control already characterized. Fit only a validated local operating region. Verify sensor sign by moving the supported object downward at fixed current: reported gap must increase. Measure false position change after a current step with the object clamped. Set measured operating range, coefficients, hover current, and candidate PD gains in config.c. Validate by recompiling and running host checks before setting calibration_ready=true.
At the nominal gap, use a catch tray, a current-limited supply, and a supported release. Tune PD for damping before adding integral. Expand the commanded range gradually. Record recovery from small disturbances and current saturation. Test the full path while refreshing web pages repeatedly to check the MCU deadline budget.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
7. Demonstrate and preserve evidence
The revised proposal targets sustainable continuous suspension and visible commanded motion with a maximum gap of 10 mm. Measure an extended run through thermal equilibrium and command motion over the validated interval, retaining the exact duration and trajectory; a finite run cannot prove indefinite operation. Check page stop, the 50 ms command watchdog, overcurrent, and physical interlock operation. Record target/estimated gap versus an independent ruler/camera reference, current, PWM, actual speed, settling time, RMS noise, and coil temperature. The former draft’s 30-second/three-target numbers are not the revised proposal specifications.
Complete the checkoff matrix, final KiCad schematics, photos, team information, and demo video. Upload/publish only when the team has reviewed the actual evidence and the instructor’s current submission requirements.

Gap and Position Control
The definitions and PI equation below record the proposal baseline. They describe a control approach to evaluate rather than a completed controller in the current sweep test.
Surface gap dd runs downward from the electromagnet’s bottom face to the suspended magnet’s top face. The proposal commits to 10–20 mm motion with a 10 g total moving mass. The force-model distance zz runs from the coil plane to the magnet center: z=d+Δgz=d+\Delta_g, where the offset depends on actual geometry.
For downward displacement, md̈=mg−F(d,i)m\ddot d=mg-F(d,i). Define e=d̂−re=\hat d-r, where rr is requested gap. The proposed controller is
u=clamp⁡(u0+Kpe+Ki∫edt,0,umax).u=\operatorname{clamp}\left(u_0+K_pe+K_i\int e\,dt,\;0,\;u_{\max}\right).
A positive error increases attraction. Duty limits, integrator anti-windup, range-checked gains, and applying both gains together at an update boundary are part of the implementation plan. Numeric gains require the measured plant and confirmed units.

title: System Design
text:
Resolution and Calibration
Both Hall sensors see the electromagnet, fixed helper magnet, and moving payload. The current acquisition uses separate ADC channels and forms a difference in the FPGA. Two sensors alone do not guarantee coil-field cancellation. Record their individual responses and sensitivities before choosing the final estimator; no installed current-sense channel is established by the latest schematic.
For calibrated differential voltage VΔ(d)V_\Delta(d), the local quantization estimate is
ΔdLSB≈Vref/4096|dVΔ/dd|.\Delta d_{\mathrm{LSB}}\approx\frac{V_{\mathrm{ref}}/4096}{|dV_\Delta/dd|}.
At the proposed 3.3 V reference, one count is approximately 0.806 mV. Measure the voltage slope across the operating range. Noise, channel skew, alignment, and calibration also limit usable resolution and accuracy. The separate November sensing notes used a 5 V ADC example; their numerical position increments do not establish performance for this 3.3 V design.
A fixed helper magnet can change the equilibrium force and force gradient. Shifting the Hall baseline does not itself improve position resolution. Check sensor headroom and calibrate the complete assembly with the helper magnet installed.

mLs4+(mR+cL)s3+(cR−kxL+kf2)s2+(kfVsKp−kxR)s+kfVsKi=0.mLs^4+(mR+cL)s^3+(cR-k_xL+k_f^2)s^2+(k_fV_sK_p-k_xR)s+k_fV_sK_i=0.
The illustrative air-core model at 10 mm center distance, with 10 g mass, 500 turns, 10 mm coil radius, R=8ΩR=8\,\Omega, L=10L=10 mH, and negligible passive damping, has a negative s2s^2 coefficient. No PI gains make that assumed continuous model strictly stable. The sampled example is also unstable. These calculations do not validate gains for the selected iron-core electromagnet.
Measure holding current, hot resistance, inductance, and local force slopes using the final payload and helper magnet. Check continuous and sampled stability, including acquisition and communication delay, before free suspension. Stable poles and position tolerance are separate checks; the proposal’s endpoint demonstration band is ±5 mm.

title: Progress Report
text:
Electromagnet and PWM testing
We assembled and tested a low-side MOSFET circuit for the electromagnet. The coil connects to the 12 V supply and the MOSFET drain, while the source connects to the common ground. The FPGA drives the gate through a resistor. A gate-to-source resistor pulls the gate down, and a flyback diode across the coil provides a recirculation path when the MOSFET switches off.
The latest schematic shows a 1 kΩ gate series resistor, a 47 kΩ gate-to-source resistor, and PWM on FPGA pad 10. The diode cathode connects to +12 V and its anode to the drain. Earlier fixed-frequency experiments used pad 36; those pin assignments should not be mixed with the current sweeper build.
The FPGA sweeper varies an 8-bit duty value up and down to exercise the output stage without position feedback. Bench discussion reported supply current rising to approximately 28 mA and falling during the sweep, with input power around 0.34 W near the reported maximum. These are approximate observations from the sweeping test rather than a rated coil-current or force measurement. They establish progress on actuation testing, while lifting force, thermal behavior, and a validated high-frequency switching waveform remain to be characterized.

MCU: GNU Arm toolchain
Install CMake, Ninja or Make, and GNU Arm Embedded GCC. Supply the device headers containing stm32l432xx.h/system_stm32l4xx.h and the CMSIS core headers containing core_cm4.h. Your course repository already contains both under lab/lab07/lab07_mcu/lab07_proj. Do not copy generated lab outputs into this repository.
From the repository root in PowerShell:
$course = '..\hmc-e155\lab\lab07\lab07_mcu\lab07_proj'
cmake -S firmware -B build/mcu -G Ninja `
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=arm-gcc.cmake `
  -DSTM32_DEVICE_INCLUDE="$((Resolve-Path "$course/STM32L4xx/Device/Include").Path)" `
  -DCMSIS_CORE_INCLUDE="$((Resolve-Path "$course/CMSIS_5/CMSIS/Core/Include").Path)"
cmake --build build/mcu
Outputs: build/mcu/maglev.elf, maglev.hex, and maglev.map. GNU extensions are used for the vector table. The linker reserves the main 48 KiB SRAM bank and at least 4 KiB stack; the separate 16 KiB SRAM2 is unused. Standard C library support is supplied by GNU Arm with nosys stubs; floating-point printf is unnecessary.
Program the HEX through ST-LINK using STM32CubeProgrammer or your lab’s established programming workflow. Select STM32L432KC, connect/reset, load the built image, verify, then run with coil power disconnected. The ST-LINK serial port is not the ESP8266 link used here.

title: Candidate hardware and proposed wiring
text:
Parts and early decision

One or two TI DRV5055 linear analog Hall sensors, initially evaluate A3 or A4 sensitivity. Set hall_sensors in firmware to match the installed count; an absent CH2 should be grounded. Choose the full ordering code/package after measuring field range. These are analog sensors, not magnetic switches. Power them at 3.3 V with local 100 nF bypassing; use the same quiet rail for the ADC reference. The manufacturer datasheet specifies the transfer range, orientation, and bandwidth. Verify package pin numbering; TO-92 and SOT-23 differ.
One MCP3204-CI/P 12-bit ADC at 3.3 V, with CH0 current, CH1 primary Hall, CH2 reference Hall, and unused CH3 tied to analog ground. See the MCP3204 datasheet. The MCU drives this ADC on SPI1, sharing clock/data lines with the FPGA and using a separate chip select.
One INA240A1 amplifier, gain 20, and a 0.100 ohm precision shunt in series with the coil. At 3.3 V, ground both REF inputs for unidirectional measurement. Account for zero-current output headroom/offset in calibration. Its datasheet describes common-mode behavior and PWM rejection. An SOIC adapter or assembled board is needed if using a bare IC.
A MOSFET with verified on-resistance at the actual gate voltage, a gate driver such as UCC27511, and a flyback diode rated above coil current and supply/transient voltage. Driver inputs, supply bypassing, and gate discharge follow its datasheet. A 5 V driver supply is a candidate, subject to the selected MOSFET.
A separate current-limited coil supply, fuse, physical E-stop, current comparator, output logic, and a nonmagnetic frame with a catch tray. Coil voltage/current, fuse, diode/clamp, MOSFET, threshold circuit, and thermal ratings remain contingent on the coil.

Start with an instructor-approved stockroom coil or one inexpensive test coil. Determine the usable gap with a force measurement and temperature test. A manufacturer’s holding force at contact does not establish levitation capacity. Check whether a permanent-magnet object rotates, sticks to the core, or produces ambiguous Hall readings. A steel-only object requires a different field identification experiment before this estimator can be adopted.
The candidate BOM contains budget allowances, not live supplier quotes. Replace all allowance values with dated quotes, full ordering numbers, stockroom availability, shipping, and tax before submitting or purchasing. The course currently marks the purchasing policy as under construction; confirm it with the instructors.
The MCP3204 pseudo-differential IN- input must remain within 100 mV of ground; do not directly connect two mid-supply Hall outputs as a differential pair. This design combines separate single-ended measurements digitally.

title: Candidate hardware and proposed wiring
text:
Power circuit connectivity
The netlist defines the circuit nodes. This is a design sketch; it must become a labeled KiCad schematic using the selected packages and ratings before the final report.
flowchart LR
    PS[Coil supply positive] --> F[Fuse / E-stop power contact]
    F --> V[Node VCOIL]
    V --> R[Inline shunt 0.100 ohm]
    R --> L[Coil]
    L --> D[MOSFET drain]
    D --> Q[MOSFET source to power ground]
    D -->|flyback: anode → cathode| V
    R -. Kelvin sense .-> A[Current amplifier]
    A --> ADC[ADC CH0]
    A --> C[Overcurrent comparator]
    C --> E[Healthy interlock]
The flyback diode cathode connects to VCOIL before the shunt. That places both coil and shunt inside the recirculation loop, so off-time current is measured. A shunt placed only in the supply lead outside that loop does not measure recirculating current. The diode protects the MOSFET but yields slow decay; measure whether this is adequate. Replacing it with a higher-voltage clamp requires rechecking MOSFET/common-mode/supply stress and retuning.
Hardware must force the driver inactive whenever PWM is low, FPGA enable is low, MCU permit is low, or the physical interlock is unhealthy. For example, use 3.3 V AND logic to combine these conditions into the driver’s noninverting input; tie its inverting input low. Keep a gate-source pulldown and logic-input pulldowns so an unconfigured FPGA cannot energize the coil. The physical E-stop also opens coil power. Derive fault_n from the E-stop auxiliary contact and an overcurrent comparator with a defined safe default; its exact schematic/threshold depends on the chosen current limit. Never tie fault_n permanently high in the powered levitator.
For the numerical example, 0.5 A produces about 1.0 V at the current amplifier, or 1241 ADC counts. A separate comparator threshold must be established from actual offsets, gain tolerance, and thermal/current ratings. FPGA sampling is not a substitute for this physical cutoff. Software shutdown removes drive; stored magnetic energy still decays through the flyback path.
